quest.title: The Color of Memory
quest.description: After all has been settled, Citlali invites you to her dwelling. It seems she's found an answer to the question that was troubling her before...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x275, Primogem x60, Mora x26025, Guide to Kindling x5, The Cornerstone of Stars and Flames x1, Hero's Wit x3, Mystic Enhancement Ore x6

chapter.num: Memories Flowing With Color: Act III
chapter.title: The Truth of the Battle of Seven Colors

talks.objective: Accompany Citlali back to her dwelling

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Now, when it comes to weaving the scroll itself, you don't actually need to lift a finger. But, if we're going to pass on Huitzilin's technique, your participation is critical.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What are you saying, Citlali?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Follow me.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, look at this place... Do you weave scrolls, too?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Scrolls...

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Scrolls? I thought you were going to show me your masterpiece?

dialogues.speaker: Huitzilin
dialogues.text: That I am, old friend. The technique I'm about to show you directly relates to woven scrolls.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: *sigh* Fine, what is it? Something that can turn the tide of war or prevent a great disaster?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: You probably want to challenge me, right? I know you don't have the strength for a real fight, so I'll let you beat me with words.

dialogues.speaker: Huitzilin
dialogues.text: *cough*... Old friend, my life is nearing its end. I'm afraid... I don't have time for another match.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Hey...

dialogues.speaker: Huitzilin
dialogues.text: Don't worry. I trust in the belief of our tribe... that death is not the end, but the beginning of a new existence in the Night Kingdom, where everything is made of memories.

dialogues.speaker: Huitzilin
dialogues.text: So, do you know why our ancestors insisted on using colorful woven scrolls to record our history?

dialogues.speaker: Huitzilin
dialogues.text: Because... history is the memory of a people.

dialogues.speaker: Huitzilin
dialogues.text: We give our scrolls an orange hue so the dead can still feel the warmth of the setting sun.

dialogues.speaker: Huitzilin
dialogues.text: We decorate them with kernels of Grainfruit so the dead can still enjoy the abundance of our harvests.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: I know that... But, something this important? Why entrust it to me and not one of your students?

dialogues.speaker: Huitzilin
dialogues.text: Hehe, as your friend, I admit... I'm being a bit selfish.

dialogues.speaker: Huitzilin
dialogues.text: *cough* I don't have long, Citlali. I'm not sure... I can truly explain my decision. But, I know you will understand one day.

dialogues.speaker: Huitzilin
dialogues.text: For now... will you accept my final request?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: ...Just this once.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: I understand now, Huitzilin — just like you said I would... Claw, help me move this outside. I'm going to color it.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon, come with me.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: We are like birds, soaring through the horizons of time...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: (Package Video)

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: I knew you would understand.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: This... This is the special scroll! How did you know how to weave it, Citlali?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Remember the "gift from the spirits"?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hold on, you've lived for more than two hundred years, you know how to weave the special scroll — that must mean... You're the one behind the "gifts from the spirits"!

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Well, it's not like I wanted to interact with the appointed, so whenever I delivered the scroll, I used illusions to confuse them.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: The fact that it turned into some kind of "divine intervention" is because no one was skilled enough to see through my tricks...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Why not just tell them?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You've carried the duty alone for all these years? Even if you don't like interacting with people, why not teach someone else how to do it?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: #...{NICKNAME}, you can see the special color, right?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Yes.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: The essence of that color is memory. That means completing the special scroll is a process of searching for color within your memories.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Passing the technique on to someone means sharing your memories with them. You need to leave traces of your color in their memory, and they must do the same.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Even though I only confirmed that today, I've had suspicions for a long time.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: And, well... ever since Huitzilin died, I haven't wanted to form that kind of connection with people.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, yeah...

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: It was her final wish, so I kind of resigned myself to taking on the burden forever. After all, I have all the time in the world.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: But, Claw never stopped appointing new candidates to weave the scroll — despite knowing exactly how I felt about the situation.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You mean, he never stopped trying to find new friends for you?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: ...I knew exactly what he was doing. And, yeah, if I ever did share my memories with someone, I guess that person would be a friend. But, it never got to that point.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: This time, though, you win, Claw.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Take this. I guess... it's my response to what you told me the other night.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What is it?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: If I had to choose my color, it would be the color of this handkerchief.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Countless people exist in my memories, and I know one day, that will be my fate, too — a memory living on in someone else's head.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Since you have a long lifespan, you're the perfect candidate to bear this memory... and carry my color in your mind.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Does this mean I'm officially your friend?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: ...Just keep it safe, and you better not forget my color when I'm gone.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, it's a little early to talk about death, don't you think? It's only been a few seconds since we made the friendship official...

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Isn't that what friends are for?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Okay, this is a serious commitment... Well, Citlali, if {NICKNAME}'s going to leave their color in your mind, too, it'll probably be gold, right?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Actually, their mark is already there. Remember the mind-reading effect I couldn't fix? Well, I finally got to the bottom of it.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Sharing senses allows communication to occur between the consciousness of different people. Naturally, memories are also involved in that process.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Although I didn't know it at the time, we both have the ability to see the "color of memory," which means that when I shared my senses with you, a connection was created between our memories.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: And that connection is what caused my original spell to go haywire...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #So... you can hear {NICKNAME}'s thoughts because you left traces of color in each other's memories?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #And that's why {NICKNAME} could hear your thoughts, too! Because it works both ways, right?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Quick thinking, but only those trained in the mystic arts can maintain that level of connection.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: #That's why I can still hear {NICKNAME}'s thoughts, but not the other way around.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: There's no need to worry, though. Now that I've figured out how it works, I'll get rid of it in no time.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh...

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: (I lied — hearing each other's thoughts actually depends on the strength of the connection between our memories.)

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: (So, after everything we just went through, I bet you can hear me again.)

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: (I knew it...)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (So, is there a way to stop it?)

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: (Since the connection between our memories is already there, the only way to get rid of the effect is for one of us to forget about the other.)

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: (Heh, just messing with you... I'm a legendary shaman of my tribe, now that I know the cause, of course I can figure out how to fix it.)

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: (It'll probably still take some time, though. So, bear with me for now.)

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: (Besides, I'm an open book. It's not like you're gonna hear anything embarrassing... Oh, um, unless I've had a few drinks.)

choices.text: (Oh, so you can turn it off? That's a shame...)

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: (A shame? I mean, if you ever miss this whole telepathy mess, I could always share my senses with you again.)

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: (No promises, though. Some thoughts are better kept to yourself.)

choices.text: (Oh, so you can turn it off? That's good to hear.)

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: (Yeah, I get what you mean. Some thoughts are better kept to yourself.)

talks.objective: Wait until morning the next day (08:00 – 12:00)
Give the woven scroll to Chief Biram

dialogues.speaker: Biram
dialogues.text: Ah, you did it? Your investigation into the Battle of Seven Colors must have been fruitful indeed. I do hope you share what you learned.

dialogues.speaker: Caholom
dialogues.text: Wow, the scroll is finished already!

dialogues.speaker: Aywastin
dialogues.text: Elder Tlapo's wisdom is never wrong!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Yeah, we should explain... Take it away, {NICKNAME}!

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You share everything you learned about the special color while keeping Citlali's contribution a secret.

dialogues.speaker: Biram
dialogues.text: I see...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You don't look surprised at all...

dialogues.speaker: Biram
dialogues.text: It makes perfect sense! History is the memory of a people. If we want to depict it, a dye derived from people's memories is, of course, the best choice.

dialogues.speaker: Biram
dialogues.text: Now, it's just a matter of preserving this secret technique...

dialogues.speaker: Biram
dialogues.text: Hmm... From your description, it sounds like learning the technique requires the previous holder to share their memories?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, yeah...

dialogues.speaker: Biram
dialogues.text: In that case, I must work with our priests to re-invent the technique based on the principles you described.

dialogues.speaker: Biram
dialogues.text: #After all, memories are precious things — meant to be shared with those closest to us. I cannot take that choice away from you, {NICKNAME}.

dialogues.speaker: Biram
dialogues.text: You completed your task admirably. Finding a way to carry on that legacy is now our duty.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Alright! We'll leave that to you!

dialogues.speaker: Biram
dialogues.text: Oh, and please pass along my thanks to Granny Itztli.

dialogues.speaker: Biram
dialogues.text: We interrogated the Fontainian merchant she apprehended, and it turns out, he is the reason some among our tribe started to question our history.

dialogues.speaker: Biram
dialogues.text: He hired people to spread misinformation about the Battle of Seven Colors. The recent friction within the tribe is entirely his doing.

dialogues.speaker: Biram
dialogues.text: We now have a record of his crimes and will begin working with Fontaine authorities in a few days.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So, he was behind the controversy in the first place! Guess it's easier to investigate when people are already questioning something...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Anyway, that clears it up! People don't just question their history out of nowhere.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Thank you, Biram. We'll be on our way.

dialogues.speaker: Biram
dialogues.text: Until we meet again.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: You told him everything, right?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yep! We left out the part about your contribution, but it kinda seemed like Chief Biram saw through us...

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: You could have just said it was a "gift from the spirits"...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Yeah, but Chief Biram deserved something in return for his hard work.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: ...I guess he is different from the previous chiefs. But, if he figures out it was me all these years, I'm in for a world of trouble.

dialogues.speaker: Allier
dialogues.text: There you are! I've been looking everywhere for you!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, it's the other Fontainian researcher... He wasn't taken away with his boss?

dialogues.speaker: Allier
dialogues.text: Please, call me Allier... After questioning, the tribe absolved me of any serious wrongdoing, so here I am.

dialogues.speaker: Allier
dialogues.text: I'll be heading back to Fontaine soon — no employer means no funding, after all. But, I wanted to finish my investigation first.

dialogues.speaker: Allier
dialogues.text: I'd like to ask some questions about Huitzilin. I want people outside of Natlan to hear her story, but my understanding still has some holes.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Questions? Hmph... Why should I let an outlander tell our stories?

dialogues.speaker: Allier
dialogues.text: Don't misunderstand — I have no intention of twisting your history or using it to make a profit. It's just honest curiosity, I assure you.

dialogues.speaker: Allier
dialogues.text: I believe amazing stories deserve to be shared with the world. Culture thrives through dialogue and exchange.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: He has a point.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Alright, you can ask your questions, but be quick. I have important plans after this.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Important plans?

dialogues.speaker: Allier
dialogues.text: Thank you very much!

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Allier conducts a thorough interview, only leaving when Citlali finally runs out of patience.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Another day, another drained social battery...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We should probably get going, then.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Mhm... Ah, hold on — you owe me a pair of books!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, that... When it comes to light novels, your memory is like a steel trap, huh...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Books that rare will take some time to find...

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: You're telling me... Yeah, it's not gonna be easy — you might need to go to Yae Publishing House in person...

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: But, I don't need them right away. Just don't forget, okay?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Of course! We'll get them sent to you as soon as we can!

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Sent to me...? Nuh-uh, I don't want a stranger knocking on my door when I'm hungover. Here, just take this.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: And this is...?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: The key to my house. Don't bother knocking next time — you'll disturb my sleep.

dialogues.speaker: Montluson
dialogues.text: My bank balance...

dialogues.speaker: Caholom
dialogues.text: Ah, Natlan's victory against the Abyss! Very fitting for a scroll like this...

dialogues.speaker: Aywastin
dialogues.text: I wonder how long until Elder Tlapo chooses the next appointed?

dialogues.speaker: Besuci
dialogues.text: Speaking of Elder Tlapo, I heard he went missing yesterday! Do you know what happened?

dialogues.speaker: Chogan
dialogues.text: Elder Tlapo works in mysterious ways. The meaning of his departure will become clear in time, but for now, we cannot hope to fathom it.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Claw helps you bring the woven scroll outside.
